Commentary.Commentary: First win of the Super 8s - Right then, England become the first team to register two points in the Super Eights phase and take the lead in Group 2, ahead of the likes of Pakistan and New Zealand. Sri Lanka, meanwhile, are the team under pressure in this group and if they falter or rain plays spoilsport in either of their remaining games, they could be heading out of the tournament. Let's now shift our focus to India, to Ahmedabad, to be precise. Super Sunday rounds off with a clash between two titans of international cricket as India take on South Africa in a Group 1 clash. That match is scheduled to start at 1.30 pm GMT and the Proteas have elected to BAT first. You can simply switch tabs and tune in to our coverage of that game. Cheers!

No demons in the pitch - England's captain, Harry Brook, says that bowling out Sri Lanka for under 100 runs is indeed a wonderful present. Feels there weren't many demons on the pitch, but the bowlers from both teams bowled really well. Highlights it was hard to time with the bat but credits the way Phil Salt played on the pitch. Admits Jos Buttler is arguably the best player in white-ball cricket, Brook feels he is lacking a bit of confidence and is not concerned about his form at all. On Will Jacks, Brook says Jacks was annoyed with the way he got out and chuckles by saying he bowls well when he is annoyed. Feels that they can play in any conditions, it's about getting a perfect start and feels they will once Jos Buttler starts firing on top.

One bad game with the bat - Sri Lanka's captain, Dasun Shanaka, says that it is very disappointing to lose like this but they did have a lot of positives with the ball. Further adds that he expected his players to bat well, which didn't happen. Reckons that the pitch was definitely on the drier side but with the lights coming into effect, it did get better. Mentions that it wasn't like the opposition bowled extremely well and it was more like the batters didn't bat up to the mark. Further applauds the bowling effort and says that they can restrict any opposition to an under-par total. Feels that it is one bad game with the bat but knows that it is not affordable in a World Cup. Ends by saying that they can still bounce back.
The two captains are now in conversation with Michael Atherton...

Let's quickly recap the first innings - After opting to bowl first, Sri Lanka came out firing with ball and had England reeling inside the Powerplay. The Lankans picked up a couple of wickets and kept the scoring rate down but it was in the middle phase that the hosts managed to put the squeeze on. Wickets at regular intervals kept pegging England back. Phil Salt, who had't gotten out of the Powerplay so far in this World Cup, managed to play a fighting knock and his 62 off 40 balls helped England get to some sort of a total. Will Jacks yet again chipped in with a crucial cameo and in the end, 146 was enough to get England over the line, that too with ease.

Player of the Match - Will Jacks gets the accolade for his brilliant all-round effort of 21 runs with the bat and then 3 for 22 with the ball. He says they are buzzing right now. Jofra Archer gave them a good start, and they managed to pick up wickets regularly. Shares that they know this ground really well, as they played a series recently. Reckons that chasing is hard at this ground with the ball turning so they were squeezing it every dot. Notes that he loves to contribute with the ball. Admits they haven't played to their best, but they are finding ways to win every match. They trust their game, play with freedom, and it's been working for them so far.

Sri Lanka's miserable outing with the bat - At the innings interval, Sri Lanka must have thought that they had the game in the bag but things turned out completely different. The approach with the bat from the top order was questionable at best and once again, we saw how much they depend on Pathum Nissanka providing those good starts. The middle order showed some fight but it wasn't anything substantial, barring that knock of 30 from the skipper, Dasun Shanaka. Sri Lanka isn't a side that is filled with all-rounders and at some point earlier in the chase, they should have thought about it. They now ave a moutain to climb if they are to make it through to the semi-finals.

England's love affair with spin continues - Since the time England have been in Sri Lanka prior to the World Cup, they have enjoyed their time with the ball and their spinners have ruled the roost to say the least. Things were set up inside the Powerplay as Jofra Archer and Will Jacks bowled 3 overs on the trot each and picked up five wickets between them, with Jacks taking a three-fer. After the Powerplay, it was all about game management and the likes of Liam Dawson and Adil Rashid did just that. Even Jamie Overton showed good prowess with the ball and picked up a wicket. Dawson and Rashid picked up two wickets each but it was the latter who got that crucial wicket of the Lankan skipper. All in all, a solid outing with the ball.

How's that for a win? England came into the Super 8s with a lot of pressure on their heads but they had a near-perfect record against Sri Lanka in T20Is over the last decade or so and that has prevailed here as well. A shocking loss for Sri Lanka, not because it is a loss but the manner of defeat is just too difficult to swallow, both for the players and the home fans.

Commentary.Commentary: Sri Lanka seem to have pressed the self-destruct button here. Dunith Wellalage walks out to face the hat-trick ball.

OUT! IN THE AIR AND GONE! Oh, dear! Pavan Rathnayake gives the bowler the charge on the very first ball, but it goes horribly wrong for him. Two in two for Will Jacks, and the start gets even better for England. Full and around the off stump, Rathnayake jumps out of the crease and fights the angle as he swings to go down the ground to a ball leaving him. Slices it off the outer half over cover, where Tom Banton runs over his left shoulder and takes the catch. Jacks is on a hat-trick.
Commentary.Howout: c Tom Banton b Will Jacks
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Will Jacks to Pavan Rathnayake, OUT! c Tom Banton b Will Jacks.

Commentary.Commentary: Two down for the Lankans in a jiffy. Pavan Rathnayake walks out to bat next.

OUT! CAUGHT AND BOWLED! The move to give Will Jacks the new ball has worked. The crowd have been silenced. Jacks pushes it through, full and on middle. Kusal steps out and looks to clip it away on the leg side with a closed bat face. The ball comes on slower than he anticipated. Mendis ends up closing the bat face early, and the ball pops back towards the bowler off a leading edge. The replays show that Jacks was starting to move towards his right after seeing Mendis close the bat face before stopping and accepting the catch around his left knee.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Will Jacks to Kusal Mendis, OUT! c & b Will Jacks.

Commentary.Commentary: Across off, Kusal reaches out in front and firms the drive to this full ball to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Will Jacks to Kusal Mendis, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and attacking the front pad. Kamil Mishara brings his bat out in front for the block. Ekes out an inside edge onto the pads and the batters sneak in a run as the ball rolls in front of square leg.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Will Jacks to Kamil Mishara, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Lovely shot and Mendis is on his way! Too straight, too full, on the pads. Kusal does not miss out. Plays it right in the gap between deep fine leg and deep square leg for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Jofra Archer to Kusal Mendis, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Full and straight, attacking the stumps, Mendis watchfully defends.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Jofra Archer to Kusal Mendis, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: The next batter is in. Kusal Mendis is in at number 3.

OUT! CAUGHT! Jamie Overton went back on the fence just before this ball, and Pathum Nissanka has picked him out. Archer serves a full ball, outside the line of the off stump. Nissanka was better off going through the off side but he opted to whip it away on the leg side. He has to drag it from outside off and he fails to get any power on the shot. Overton is looking into the sun but he moves to his left in the deep and takes a safe catch over his head. A big wicket for England.
Commentary.Howout: c Jamie Overton b Jofra Archer
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Jofra Archer to Pathum Nissanka, OUT! c Jamie Overton b Jofra Archer.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries! Archer strays on the pads, full in length. Nissanka crouches and goes for the sweep. Gets it finer than he would have intended and the ball beats Jos Buttler to his left.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Jofra Archer to Pathum Nissanka, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Nicely done! Archer hits the deck hard, over middle and leg. Nissanka takes a step away from the stumps and plays it very late to find the gap. He uses the pace and glides it off the leg stump to the left of backward point for a four.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Jofra Archer to Pathum Nissanka, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Pitched up, on middle and leg, Pathum Nissanka charges down the track but fails to get under the ball. He can only hit it along the ground to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Jofra Archer to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: In and around the off pole, Mishara hangs back and angles it from the crease to backward point. A good comeback from Jacks after conceding a boundary on the first ball.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Will Jacks to Kamil Mishara, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller now, in line with the off stump. Kamil presses half-forward to meet the ball. Bunts it off the inner half to the left of the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Will Jacks to Kamil Mishara, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short and outside off, there to be put away. Mishara hops back and slaps it hard but picks out the cover-point fielder.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Will Jacks to Kamil Mishara, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Flatter and shorter, on off, Mishara pats it off the back foot to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Will Jacks to Kamil Mishara, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Jacob Bethell cuts it off this time! Around off, on a good length, Kamil thumps it from the crease towards cover-point. A favourable bounce for Bethell this time and he dives to parry it towards the point fielder.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Will Jacks to Kamil Mishara, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! That should have been stopped! Will Jacks shares the new ball with Archer. Tossed up, on a nagging length, a hint of turn, Kamil waits on the back foot and punches it to cover-point, where Jacob Bethell moves to his right and dives. The ball goes under his hands and goes away for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Will Jacks to Kamil Mishara, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Full and at the sticks, leaving the left-hander. Kamil Mishara pushes out in front of his body with hard hands. The ball squirts off an outside edge to deep backward point. Mishara is also underway with a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Jofra Archer to Kamil Mishara, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: A tidy over so far.
Wide! A tight call, but it goes against the bowler. Archer is not happy one bit. Moving away, flirting wih the guideline, on a good length. Kamil extends his hands to flay it away but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Jofra Archer to Kamil Mishara, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Going across the left-hander but it sneaks just inside the tramline. Kamil Mishara lets it be. Jos Buttler dives to his left to gather the ball.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Jofra Archer to Kamil Mishara, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pace off, full and on the pads. Pathum Nissanka clips it square on the leg side and gets off the mark with a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Jofra Archer to Pathum Nissanka, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Slip has disappeared after 2 balls. Angled into the right-hander, on a hard length. Nissanka looks to get it up and over short fine leg but the ball climbs onto him. The ball catches him on the forearm before deflecting onto the shoulder and then it drops on the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Jofra Archer to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hits the top of off, does Jofra, on a back of a length. Nissanka hops and taps it back on the deck.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Jofra Archer to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A swing and a miss first up! Archer steams in from over the wicket and bashes the surface, outside off. Nissanka gets on his toes and swivels for the pull but the ball goes under his bat.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Jofra Archer to Pathum Nissanka, No run.
